Consider the function $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}+x$ which is defined and continuous on the closed interval $[1,8].$ By filling the blank spaces in the sentence below, complete the statement of the intermediate value theorem:

*If $k$ is a number that lies between $\text{ ________ }$ inclusively, then there exists a number $c\in [1,8]$ such that $f(c)=k.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[1,8],$ so the intermediate value theorem guarantees that $f(x)=k$ has a solution for each value of $k$ between $f(1)$ and $f(8).$

Since $f(1)=2$ and $f(8)=10$, we must have 
$k\in [2,10].$

Therefore, the missing part is "$2$ and $10$".
